descriptions.success: Under the silk canopy, {worker_name} has sex with the noble while imagining your voice at the bedside. descriptions.success: A noble of the inner circle offers {worker_name} an apartment in the east wing, a stipend, and a ring of office: a kept life above the snow line of the court. {worker_name} declines with perfect courtesy and one unspoken reason, which is you. The noble, fascinated by the refusal, pays for the evening twice over.
descriptions.critical_success: The refusal is so graceful the story crosses the castle by morning: somewhere out in the city is a person worth more than the east wing. Half the court requests {worker_name} that week just to look at devotion up close, and the bookings come home to your ledger.
descriptions.mediocre: {worker_name} asks for a night to think the offer over, and the hesitation costs the evening its shine. The answer is still no, but it arrives sounding like arithmetic instead of loyalty.
descriptions.failure: For one long moment above the castle gardens {worker_name} almost says yes, and knows it, and comes home shaken. The near-yes sits between you like a third person at the table, and the noble's withdrawn favor costs the house besides.

descriptions.success: Your house's concession at the castle comes up for renewal, and a rival house has spent all winter buying the steward's ear. {worker_name} spends the appointment doing quiet work between the pleasantries, a doubt seeded there, a compliment placed there, because your contract is half a home now. The renewal is signed by the end of the week.
descriptions.critical_success: {worker_name} does better than defend the contract: the steward, thoroughly charmed, extends it two seasons and adds the winter feasts to the schedule. Afterward {worker_name} finds you to plan how to staff it, partner to partner.
descriptions.mediocre: The lobbying lands soft. The contract survives on its own merits, and {worker_name}'s effort neither helps nor hurts the outcome.
descriptions.failure: {worker_name} pushes the house's case one sentence too far, and the steward wonders aloud why a pleasure servant is talking terms. The overstep costs a fine and a season of frost, and what stings {worker_name} most is having made your position worse while trying to help.

descriptions.success: The castle returns workers for a wrong bow the way other clients return cold soup. Knowing what a wasted hire costs you, {worker_name} spends the carriage ride drilling your newest recruit: which titles, which doors, which silences. The newcomer passes the doorward's inspection and earns a first night instead of a dismissal.
descriptions.critical_success: The coaching takes so well that the newcomer draws a repeat request from a senior courtier on the very first evening. {worker_name} hands you a second castle earner inside a week and shrugs off the thanks, pleased mostly by the look on your face.
descriptions.mediocre: The drilling helps a little. The newcomer survives the doors but earns only the minimum, nerves eating most of the polish.
descriptions.failure: Half-learned protocol proves worse than none. The newcomer mangles a dignitary's title at the threshold and both workers are sent home before the first candle burns down, and the castle bills your house for the empty chamber. {worker_name} takes it hard, certain of having failed you and the recruit both.

descriptions.success: After an oil-slick handjob brings the courtier to orgasm, a gold pin appears under the sheet as a private reward. {worker_name} sends the booked fee to your ledger, then slips the pin into a boot. The palace records the service; neither the steward nor you records the gift.
descriptions.critical_success: {worker_name} edges the courtier with slow hands until one climax breaks into a second. A jeweled clasp joins the fee on the bedside table, but only the fee reaches your books. The clasp disappears beneath {worker_name}'s clothes, a profitable little rebellion hidden behind immaculate service.
descriptions.mediocre: The gift turns out to be plated tin, hardly worth the risk of pocketing it, and the evening's honest earnings are ordinary.
descriptions.failure: The steward inventories everything, including what courtiers wear into a chamber and do not wear out of it. The missing pin surfaces by morning, the questions land on your house, and the fine for smuggled favors comes out of your strongbox.

descriptions.success: The evening's list says the treasury minister, dull as ledger paper, at the ninth bell. {worker_name} quietly trades the slot for a livelier young courtier, protocol unconsulted and you unconsulted too. The courtier pays cheerfully, and the minister, this once, never learns of it.
descriptions.critical_success: The swapped-in courtier arrives with two friends and a purse apiece, and the reshuffled evening outearns the official list by half. {worker_name} regrets nothing, which worries you a little.
descriptions.mediocre: The trade gains nothing. The substitute client is pleasant, pays the standard rate, and the risk buys no reward at all.
descriptions.failure: Treasury ministers keep accounts of everything, including slights. The formal complaint reaches the Governor's office by morning, and the penalty for a broken appointment, plus the cost of soothing the minister, comes straight out of your season's profit.

descriptions.success: {worker_name} enters the noble's bed as an envoy for the house you are building. Love for you sharpens the sex: patient foreplay, deep thrusts, and a climax timed with practiced care. The delighted client books a month ahead, and every advance goes straight into your vault.

descriptions.failure: Midway through the evening the noble goes still, tilts {worker_name}'s chin toward the candle, and studies what is written there. A look like that has an owner, the noble says, and it is not anyone in this castle. The night is released unpaid, discreet and oddly gentle, and {worker_name} walks home to you with empty hands and no regrets.

The cuffs, commands, oral service, and hard penetration stay inside limits agreed before the door closed. Thinking of your face steadies every response until the client climaxes, satisfied, and pays without complaint.

That devotion carries the session through a brutal final climax. The client pays double; {worker_name} returns intact and proud to your door.

The old tyrant, who has broken workers for less, unbuckles the straps in silence and says only: go home to them. No fee, no punishment, and the strangest mercy the castle has ever shown.

The nobles pay for {worker_name}'s evenings; you get the part of them that matters.

You bid on the tender three days before your rivals know it exists and win it at leisure. {worker_name} refuses any cut of it, on the grounds that watching your rivals lose was payment enough.

descriptions.critical_success: {worker_name} does not just kill the rumor but follows it upstream, and comes home with the name of the rival house that started it, written on the back of a stolen invitation. You now owe your best friend a very good dinner, and you both know it.
